title: Modulation of iron metabolism by new chemicals interacting with the iron regulatory system
summary: AI-guided ligand selection and cell experiments identified V004-0872 as an inhibitor of the IRP–IRE interaction. Experiments implicated IRP2 Cys512 and linked inhibition to altered transferrin-receptor and ferritin expression and reduced cellular iron. This is a cellular mechanism result, not evidence of therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: AI-based ligand design ranked candidate IRP2-binding chemicals from a library for experimental screening; the model-guided selection led to compounds used to identify a previously unreported chemical inhibition mechanism.
organization: University of California, Berkeley; University of Chicago; University of California, Santa Barbara

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; primary publication record or first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Cell assays tested candidate compounds and chemical analogues, including loss of activity for a chloropropanamide analogue, and examined IRP2 Cys512 and iron-regulatory protein expression.
evidence.unknown: Cellular experiments do not establish safety, in-vivo activity or therapeutic benefit.
evidence.ai_role: AI-based ligand design ranked candidate IRP2-binding chemicals from a library for experimental screening; the model-guided selection led to compounds used to identify a previously unreported chemical inhibition mechanism.
